findings.title: Malformed half-paired RPC identity is elevated to local administrator
findings.evidence: authority() rejects clientId present without clientDeviceId, but determines local authority solely from clientId being undefined. A context with clientDeviceId populated and clientId missing therefore receives {kind:"local",id:"local"}; privileged jobs.registerProject/jobs.setDispatch handlers accept this principal. Neither half-populated identity shape fails closed.
findings.reproduction: Handler-level fake-service probe with context {runtime:{},cloudJobs:fakeService,clientDeviceId:"attacker-device"} observed registerProject return {registered:true} and fake service receive principal {kind:"local",id:"local"}.
findings.requested_change: Reject any context where exactly one of clientId/clientDeviceId is present, and require an explicit trusted local-principal marker for local admin authority; add regressions for each partial shape and prove no privileged callback runs.
findings.reachability_limit: Current production runtime injection/mobile grants are not wired, so this does not establish an externally reachable live exploit; it is a source-level authorization-boundary defect that must be closed before integration.

findings.title: Runtime identity is not revalidated between inbox check and terminal input
findings.evidence: notify() validates inbox response _meta.runtimeId once, then performs terminal send --text, waits, and terminal send --enter without checking that either command still targets the same runtime. A restart/rebind after the check can direct a stale notification to a different terminal session.
findings.reproduction: Hermetic mocked-run probe returned runtimeId=current for inbox, changed simulated runtime to restarted-before-input on text send, and still observed notify_return=true with both terminal-send commands; call runtimes were [current,current,restarted-before-input].
findings.requested_change: Revalidate the runtime binding immediately before each terminal input (including before Enter), or use a transport operation that atomically binds validation and input; add restart-between-check-and-send and restart-between-text-and-Enter regressions.

findings.title: Cancellation signals a numeric process group after its recorded owner can disappear or be replaced
findings.evidence: cancelAttempt initially validates recorded PID start time and process group at cancellation.ts:38-47. It then captures descendants, writes the journal, and sends SIGTERM to the saved numeric PGID at lines 58-61. After a grace delay it checks only groupExists(PGID) before sending SIGKILL at lines 65-68. signalGroup directly calls process.kill(-pgid, signal) without validating that the recorded PID/start identity or a recorded descendant still belongs to that group. If the original group exits after initial validation and before either signal, and the numeric PGID is reused, the signal can target an unrelated process group. groupExists cannot distinguish reuse. terminateOwnedAttempt already uses root/known-member identity checks before process-group signals, but cancelAttempt bypasses that guard.
findings.reproduction: Source-trace race: pause cancellation after the initial identity check (or after SIGTERM grace begins), let the recorded process group fully exit, then arrange for a different process group to acquire the same numeric PGID before the subsequent signal. The cancellation path will issue process.kill(-savedPGID, SIGTERM/SIGKILL) to that replacement group. No dynamic process reproduction was attempted under the explicit restricted-ps/source-only review boundary.
findings.impact: A stale durable attempt could cause cancellation to signal unrelated processes after process-group ID reuse, violating the executor ownership boundary.
findings.requested_change: Route both cancellation signals through an ownership-checked group-signal helper that rechecks the recorded leader PID/start/group and/or a still-matching recorded group member immediately before each signal, and fail closed when no owner identity anchors the PGID. Add an injectable or hermetic regression that removes/replaces the original identity between initial validation and TERM/KILL and asserts no signal is sent to an unowned PGID. Keep the reservation ambiguous/held on uncertainty.

seams_reviewed.recovered_lock_adoption: The recovery guard is exclusive; it checks live same-boot PID/start identity, invokes an adoption predicate, rereads lockId, renames the prior owner to a claim file, verifies the claimed identity, and installs a new owner without deleting a changed lock. Recovered execution requires the journaled process identity and server reconcile result before reserving/adopting. No additional finding in the normal valid-owner path.
seams_reviewed.late_heartbeat: Both active and recovered watchers serialize heartbeats, validate monotonic lease receipts, re-read current journal identity/phase/token after await, write only if current lease still matches, and drain/fence pending heartbeat work before settlement. The included blocked-heartbeat regression verifies an advanced journal is not overwritten.
seams_reviewed.journal_errors: Journal writes use a unique exclusive temp file and atomic rename; corrupt reads fence work. Recovered watcher catches/finalizes errors, records a bounded recoveryError when possible, resolves the drain lifecycle, and retains reservations when journal state cannot prove settlement. Existing finalizer regression covers replaced lock identity.
seams_reviewed.cancellation: Lease/attempt ownership and process identity are checked before destructive action, and unknown identity or failed stop acknowledgement retains ambiguity; however, the numeric PGID reuse race above remains.

findings.title: Short key writes can be published as the durable key before completeness is verified.
findings.evidence: The key is written with one writeSync(fd, generated, 0, KEY_BYTES, 0) call whose return value is ignored. findings.reproduction: Filesystem writeSync may legally complete fewer bytes than requested without throwing. On a short return (<32), the current path proceeds through fsync and linkSync, publishing a short key; the immediately following readKeyFile rejects it. No forced short-write test or filesystem mutation was run in this source-only review.
findings.impact: A transient short write can leave a permanent invalid key file at the canonical path and prevent restart/decryption, despite the atomic-publication contract.
findings.requested_change: Loop until all 32 bytes are written, treating zero progress as an error, and verify temporary key file size/content before linkSync publishes it. Add a hermetic short-write regression proving incomplete temp data is never linked as lease-sealer.key and temporary cleanup remains safe.

findings.title: Cursor use, session capacity, and service close are not synchronized with in-flight work.
findings.evidence: Continuation reads the session at line 103, then awaits registry authorization at lines 171-176 before deleting the cursor at line 187. Two calls can therefore retrieve the same cursor/session and concurrently advance the same scan. New scans check sessions.size at lines 113-115 but reserve no slot before awaiting authorization or opening the root, so concurrent requests exceed maxSessions. close() only closes sessions already in the map and has no closed state or registry of pending scans; a request already awaiting authorization can continue after close().
findings.reproduction: A temporary controlled-provider Vitest harness held two continuation authorization promises and released them together: both requests returned partial pages from the same scan with distinct cursors. findings.title: Directory identity checks validate the pathname, not the directory handle actually opened; POSIX backslash names are rewritten into different paths.

If a directory is replaced during opendir and the path restored before the second pathname check, the frame can retain a handle to the replaced directory while both checks pass. The injected filesystem reproduction returned an outside handle while all path checks reported the original child, and the scanner consumed that handle. Separately, normalizeRelativePath replaces every literal backslash with '/', although backslash is a legal POSIX filename character, so emitted relativePath can identify a different file or collide with an actual nested path.
findings.reproduction: Injected the outside directory handle only for opendir(child), leaving lstat, realpath, and stat pointed at the legitimate child. The scan accepted it and counted the outside entry. findings.title: Root identity conversion can lose inode precision before the descriptor bridge compares identity.
findings.evidence: fileIdentity stringifies values received from fs Stats; the lstat/stat calls use default bigint:false. JavaScript Number cannot exactly represent every integer above 2^53. primary_source_analysis.facts: The APFS reference says new ephemeral and virtual object identifiers must be monotonically increasing (p.12); apfs_next_obj_id is the next identifier assigned to a file-system object (p.55); the volume has a UUID (p.56); and j_inode_key_t's object identifier is the file-system object's identifier, also its inode number (p.73).
primary_source_analysis.interpretation: This supports native APFS inode number as an incarnation discriminator within one exact APFS volume: the inode is the file-system object ID allocated from the monotonically increasing object-ID sequence. This is an inference across those documented structures, not a claim about HFS, network volumes, or arbitrary Mac filesystems. The 1000-trial ROOT result is consistent with that contract.

primary_source_analysis.facts: Current Darwin man page defines fgetattrlist(fd, ... ) as returning attributes for the object represented by that fd. ATTR_CMN_FILEID is a uint64_t unique within the volume; ATTR_VOL_UUID is a UUID identifying the filesystem; ATTR_VOL_FSTYPENAME is UTF-8 filesystem type name. ATTR_CMN_GEN_COUNT instead tracks modifications to file data and may change normally; document ID is sticky to the path and survives replacement, so neither is an inode incarnation token.
primary_source_analysis.interpretation: A no-write provider can obtain the selected object identity from the already-open descriptor (uint64 fileID/inode) and the volume scope/type from fgetattrlist on that same fd. Because common fileID and volume attributes have different attribute groups/constraints, implementation may make separate calls on the same fd; validate result masks, buffer lengths, UUID, type, and exact integer width. ROOT's combined returned-attributes plus volume call is real local evidence, but production code should follow documented request constraints and verify the exact masks it requested.

primary_source_analysis.facts: The ext4 documentation states i_generation is normally changed only when a new inode is created and is particularly useful for network filesystems; EXT4_IOC_GETVERSION reads it and SETVERSION writes it.
primary_source_analysis.interpretation: The 1000-trial ROOT result supports an explicit ext4 practical incarnation provider using filesystem identity + full 32-bit i_generation (and dev/ino binding). This is not universal Linux behavior: reject non-ext4/unknown FS or unsupported/zero values. Never use SETVERSION.

updated_provider_contract.macos_apfs: On an opened no-follow directory fd, require native filesystem type exactly apfs, nonzero 16-byte ATTR_VOL_UUID, and exact unsigned 64-bit ATTR_CMN_FILEID/st_ino from that same fd. Store versioned token {provider: darwin-apfs-volume-inode-v1, volumeUuid, fileId}; verify by reopening the selected path without following symlinks and comparing all fields. Do not use st_gen or gen_count.
updated_provider_contract.linux_ext4: On an opened no-follow directory fd, require positively identified ext4, exact filesystem/device identity plus dev/ino and nonzero 32-bit FS_IOC_GETVERSION; store a versioned ext4 provider token. updated_provider_contract.limits: Practical assurance assumes trusted, normally mounted filesystems. Privileged malicious SETVERSION, raw filesystem edits/restores, cloned/replayed volume images, or APFS rollback/snapshot restoration outside normal allocation lifecycle can violate continuity assumptions; invalidate/re-enroll when volume identity or provider context changes. This is not an arbitrary-filesystem or hostile-kernel proof.

review_scope: six strict typed surfaces and trust boundary
current evaluated deployment gate and default-unavailable provider
passed_findings: Six surface-specific strict schemas bound caller input to identifiers and keep trusted facts in the injected main-process authority reader.
Provider defaults unavailable; gate schema and evaluated state are strict, and provider output checks labels, probability normalization, digest and provenance.
Current gate and authority are reread after inference; the full current gate digest is compared with the inference gate before accepting an uncached result.
C08 synthetic aggregate is not promoted as deployment evidence; no model/provider/runtime deployment is established.
Deterministic veto code refuses the reviewed hard-failure, permission, eligibility, dependency, storage-authority and evidence-incomplete cases.

verification.runtime: Node v24.18.0; Vitest 4.1.5; immutable review copy with canonical node_modules symlink; maxWorkers=1.
verification.temporary_reproduction_result: 3 controlled tests passed against immutable sources: never-settling authority.read remained pending beyond configured inference deadline; raising the current gate confidence threshold from 0.80 to 0.95 returned the old cached 0.90 suggestion without a second provider call; an abort-ignoring provider with maxConcurrent=1 received a second distinct request after the first call timed out while its promise remained unresolved.
verification.temporary_harness: /private/tmp/c09-review-repro/repro.test.ts; outside repository and not retained as product source.

findings.title: Deadline and admission bounds do not cover authority, provider availability, or gate reads; abort-ignoring provider calls release capacity while still running.
findings.evidence: advise awaits authority.read, provider.availability, and deploymentGate.current before quota, active-request deduplication, inFlight reservation, or any deadline. The post-inference deploymentGate.current and authority.read awaits are also outside the provider Promise.race. A controlled authority.read promise remained pending past deadlineMs. execute races only provider.decide against the deadline; finally decrements inFlight immediately after timeout even if decide ignores AbortSignal and remains pending. A controlled maxConcurrent=1 test timed out one never-settling provider then observed a second distinct provider call while the first promise remained unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Put all authority/gate/provider awaits under an end-to-end deadline and admission budget; deduplicate/reserve before unbounded awaits. Keep capacity charged to unresolved provider work after abort, or quarantine the provider instance and refuse new inference until settlement/confirmed termination. Ensure post-inference rechecks cannot hang indefinitely.

findings.title: Cache key omits current gate identity and threshold values, so a changed accepted gate reuses a suggestion evaluated under the prior gate.
findings.evidence: makeProviderRequest digest binds sourceRevision, checkpointRevision, evaluationReportSha256, and policyVersion but omits deploymentId, issuedAt/expiresAt, confidenceThresholds, sample counts, and other gate decision fields. The service validates current gate expiry/schema, then looks up cache by this request digest without comparing current gate to the gate stored with the cached result. Temporary controlled test produced a 0.90 suggestion at threshold 0.80, changed the current gate threshold to 0.95, and received the cached suggestion with no second provider call.
findings.requested_change: Bind a canonical digest of the complete accepted gate into cache and in-flight dedup identity (and ensure result/cache provenance records that gate identity); re-evaluate the confidence threshold on cache hits. Add threshold, deployment replacement, expiry and gate-field cache regressions.

findings.title: A relative journal path can synchronously loop forever.
findings.evidence: For a journal path such as journal.jsonl, dirname(filePath) is ".". assertPrivateDirectory sets current="."; parse(".").root is "/"; dirname(".") is again ".", so its ancestor loop never progresses. The file-path constructor accepts relative paths and does not reject them.
findings.requested_change: Require an absolute normalized journal path before directory creation/verification, and add a bounded regression asserting relative paths fail closed promptly. Also validate non-progressing ancestor traversal as a defensive invariant.

findings.title: Journal hash-chain read/append is not atomic across processes or instances sharing the file.
findings.evidence: append() verifies the current tail, computes previousHash, then separately opens O_APPEND and writes; no exclusive writer lock or compare-and-append check covers the read-chain/write transaction. O_APPEND only appends bytes; it does not serialize the preceding verify/read-modify-write, so concurrent writers can both append records with the same previousHash and permanently fail subsequent verification. The current main entrypoint has an Electron single-instance lock, but its diagnostic bypass is explicit and the C09 journal is not yet wired to a single exclusive owner; that external assumption is not enforced by this journal API.
findings.requested_change: Serialize the entire verify-plus-append transaction with a private per-journal interprocess lock or equivalent atomic writer protocol, fail closed on lock timeout/stale ownership, and add a two-process controlled writer regression. Alternatively prove and enforce one exclusive journal owner at the composition boundary, including single-instance bypass behavior, before constructing the service.

limits: The four frozen suites and temporary harness establish source-contract behavior only, not production runtime wiring, provider/model quality, real inference, deployment, privacy acceptance, accuracy, latency, or physical-device acceptance.
The relative-path hang was confirmed by direct control-flow inspection rather than invoked, because invoking it would spin synchronously and stall the test process.
The cross-process journal fork was confirmed by the unprotected read-verify-append sequence; no non-deterministic multi-process race was launched during this read-only review.
c09_foundation_review.next_action: BUILD2 to address the four blockers and add focused regressions, refresh exact source hashes, and request independent re-review. Do not mark C09 deployed or accepted from this foundation review.

c07_preview_contract_independent_review.reviewer: RESEARCH read-only comparison of FIXER C07 preview proposal with current canonical sources
c07_preview_contract_independent_review.head: a8d6be50e7527b545b969f338d76dc7c41c36f56

existing_contract_evidence.finding: CatalogEntrySchema is strict and currently has no file-version token; it includes metadata only and contentDigestSha256 is literal null.
entryId is deterministic SHA-256(rootId + NUL + NFC-normalized relative path); it is not a secret, content digest, or server-issued proof that the caller-selected path was listed.
Browse access is currently a single allowedDeviceIds list; grants are checked against paired IDs and generation rotates on access changes/reselection. There is no separate preview grant.
RPC derives desktop from authenticatedLocal, otherwise derives device principal from clientDeviceId; it does not currently enforce device scope for catalog methods.
Only mobile-scope clients are constrained by MOBILE_RPC_METHOD_ALLOWLIST; runtime-scope clients are not restricted by that allowlist.
The paired-device callback includes all last-seen DeviceRegistry entries without filtering scope; any new preview grant must explicitly distinguish mobile from runtime scope.

Native-helper timeouts fail the transport, kill its owned child, and track confirmed exit; bridge recovery refuses a fresh transport until prior exit is confirmed. Generic runBounded wrappers alone do not guarantee underlying async work has stopped.
Current listing state is keyed by target/host, root, and generation and uses request sequence guards; no file-preview state or complete-chunk client assembly exists.
Current catalog roots/page methods are mobile-allowlisted reads; files.readPreview is a separate existing method and must not be reused for registered roots.

findings.title: Caller entryId and relativePath are not proof of a listed entry
findings.evidence: The current entryId is a deterministic hash of root ID and normalized relative path. The proposed preview request accepts both entryId and relativePath, so a client can recompute an ID and request any path that passes root-relative checks; no server-side catalog membership or preview-selection token is defined. This does not itself escape the registered root, but it broadens access beyond a selected/listed entry and makes entryId look like authorization when it is not.
findings.required_correction: Choose and state whether a per-root preview grant intentionally permits every eligible file or only files emitted by the metadata catalog. For selected-entry-only semantics, issue a short-lived server-authenticated entry reference (or bounded server-side selection record) bound to authenticated principal, root ID/native incarnation, registration generation, entry ID, exact relative components and fileVersion; never trust caller absolute paths or the deterministic entryId alone. Re-resolve/verify this reference before each chunk.
findings.owner_recommendation: Main catalog preview service and shared contract owner; coordinate entry-reference issuance with metadata scanner owner.
tests: Forge entryId for an unlisted .md path and deny with no helper read.
Replay reference as another principal, root generation, root incarnation, or after TTL and deny.
Use listed entry with caller-substituted relativePath/version and deny.

findings.title: The existing authenticated principal model does not prove a phone scope
findings.evidence: data-catalog.ts maps any context.clientDeviceId to device:<id>; runtime-rpc only applies MOBILE_RPC_METHOD_ALLOWLIST to device.scope=mobile. The pairedDevices callback in main filters lastSeenAt but not DeviceEntry.scope. A new preview method that checks only the device ID or paired list could therefore treat a runtime-scope client as a phone. Current catalog grants are browse-only and there is no preview grant.
findings.required_correction: At the RPC boundary require either authenticatedLocal===true for the local desktop UI or context.clientKind===mobile with server-derived clientDeviceId; explicitly deny runtime-scope and missing-scope peers unless a separately specified trusted desktop-remote capability is approved. Add the preview method to the mobile allowlist and method-class map only as a read transport gate; independently require an explicit per-root allowedPreviewDeviceIds grant plus current paired-mobile status and the existing browse grant. The local-only setPreviewAccess mutation must require authenticatedLocal and must not be mobile-allowlisted. Do not fall back to files.readPreview.
findings.owner_recommendation: Runtime RPC/auth owner and root-enrollment store owner; FIXER to verify server-derived scope and no downgrade path.
tests: Authenticated local succeeds only after explicit UI action and root policy permits it.
Mobile without either per-root browse or preview grant is denied; revoked/unpaired device denied.
Runtime-scope device with same device ID and forged principal parameter is denied.
Remote setPreviewAccess/remove-root attempts are denied; old host unknown-method response does not fall back to worktree file reads.

findings.title: Revocation cannot clear an already displayed preview without a client notification or lease
findings.evidence: Enrollment updates rotate generation and current list hooks key state by host/root/generation, but no catalog change subscription or preview revocation event exists. Per-chunk authorization can stop future bytes, but a completed file remains in client memory/UI after a remote grant revoke until roots are refreshed or the view is otherwise replaced. Delivered bytes cannot be recalled.
findings.required_correction: Define revocation semantics honestly: each chunk rechecks registration generation, native root identity, active pairing, browse grant and distinct preview grant before and after helper awaits; stop immediately on mismatch. Add a bounded revocation/change notification or short preview lease with refresh while visible so UI clears promptly, and clear text on host/root/generation switch, disconnect, denial, close and expiry. Document that already delivered content cannot be recalled from a client.
findings.owner_recommendation: Root enrollment/event owner plus desktop and phone UI owners.
tests: Pause chunk read, revoke/unpair/replace root, then release and assert no bytes returned.
Revoke while a completed preview is visible and assert event/lease clears content within its specified bound.
Late old-host/root/generation response is discarded after a switch.

findings.title: The proposed stat version needs a precise ordinary-change guarantee and native metadata wiring
findings.evidence: MetadataEntryStat currently carries only dev/ino, size and modifiedAtMs; Python _entry_stat rounds mtime to milliseconds. No ctime_ns, mtime_ns, or fileVersion reaches the catalog entry. The proposed SHA-256 of stat fields is not a content digest and can only detect changes represented by those fields under the documented filesystem/provider assumptions.
findings.required_correction: Extend native metadata DTOs using full-width integers/canonical decimal strings for size, mtime_ns and ctime_ns, include dev/ino, file type, root generation in the version input, and expose an opaque canonical SHA-256 token in strict entry/result schemas for regular text files. Compute/compare from native no-follow stat/fstat, not rounded JS numbers. State explicitly it is a stat-version, not cryptographic content integrity; do not claim it proves bytes are unchanged against privileged metadata restoration. Bind every chunk and the entire client assembly to exactly the original version; any mismatch discards all buffered text and requires a fresh listing.
findings.owner_recommendation: Descriptor bridge/native protocol owner and catalog metadata/shared schema owner.
tests: Rewrite same file with same byte length and verify ordinary mtime/ctime change invalidates token.
Replace file inode/path and verify token mismatch; preserve normal metadata and ensure root generation mismatch rejects.
Assert full-width ns values survive JSON DTO without Number precision loss.
Verify no content hash/backup assertion is fabricated.

findings.title: FIFO replacement can block the helper before it discovers the opened object is not a regular file
findings.evidence: The proposal says final open uses O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW then checks type/version. Opening a FIFO O_RDONLY may block before fstat; the existing helper has bounded request size and the Node transport kills a timed-out child, but that is a avoidable denial of service and cleanup may remain unconfirmed.
findings.required_correction: Open final components with O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK, then fstat the opened descriptor and accept only a regular file on the registered root device; verify named parent-relative identity/version before and after bounded pread, and close in finally. Do not fall back to path-only fs reads. Keep helper timeout kill/confirmed-exit/no-overlap behavior; if exit is unconfirmed, deny future previews rather than start another helper.
findings.owner_recommendation: Native descriptor bridge owner, coordinated with preview service.
tests: Race regular file to FIFO immediately before open; operation returns bounded refusal and helper remains healthy or is killed/confirmed before reuse.
Intermediate/final symlink, socket, device, directory, cross-device mount and replaced parent reject without reading.
Ignore cancellation/hold helper beyond deadline: request settles unavailable, no second process overlaps, dispose returns boundedly, and unconfirmed cleanup blocks recovery.

findings.title: Chunk transport must enforce one ordered, bounded complete-file assembly before display
findings.evidence: The proposal specifies 16 KiB chunks, 256 KiB file cap and a 64 KiB JSON response, but does not define a server-side preview session/expected offset or a response schema that makes gaps, duplicates, interleaving, version changes and incomplete termination impossible. A caller can issue arbitrary offsets in parallel unless the service reserves per-principal capacity. UTF-8 can span chunk boundaries.
findings.required_correction: Define strict discriminated request/result schemas with an opaque previewSessionId bound to principal/connection, entry reference, root generation, fileVersion and expiry; store expectedOffset, exact total bytes and concurrency reservation server-side. Require contiguous monotonic offsets, exact byte count/nextOffset, stable total/version across every chunk, max 16 KiB raw, max 256 KiB full file and wire output below 64 KiB; cap per-client/global sessions and deadline. Use canonical base64 with decoded length validation. Clients concatenate bounded raw bytes and perform fatal UTF-8 decoding only after final chunk; render nothing until final version/authorization checks pass.
findings.owner_recommendation: Main preview service/shared DTO/RPC owner plus desktop and mobile client owners.
tests: Exact maximum and max+1 sizes; exact/final partial chunk boundaries; malformed/noncanonical base64 and oversized wire.
Duplicate, skipped, reordered, concurrent and cross-session offsets reject; no mixed version or partial text rendered.
UTF-8 multibyte character split across chunks succeeds after final assembly; invalid UTF-8 and binary reject with no partial display.
No automatic read during listing; explicit click only; no Markdown/HTML/link/image/external resource execution.

findings.title: Privacy and focus acceptance must cover transport logs and late UI responses
findings.evidence: Current catalog results expose relative metadata only; current desktop and phone listing hooks are host/root/generation keyed and suppress stale list responses. There is no preview path yet, so those guarantees do not automatically cover preview bytes or errors. RPC feature-interaction recording currently has no data-catalog special case, but new generic logging/telemetry must not record params or result contents.
findings.required_correction: Return no canonical paths, raw file bytes outside the bounded chunk DTO, auth material, or sensitive file names in errors/telemetry. Never persist preview text in catalog registry, feature-interaction logs, crash logs, Laya/advisory input, or agent context. Render escaped plain text only; clear on host/root/generation/revoke/disconnect/expiry and guard every completion with a monotonically increasing request token. Do not focus or activate another host, worktree, terminal, tab, or external editor.
findings.owner_recommendation: Shared RPC/observability owner and desktop/mobile UI owners.
tests: Capture diagnostics/feature interactions and assert they exclude raw content, absolute path and auth token.
Switch hosts while delayed chunks resolve; old response never appears or changes selected host/focus.
Grant revocation, close, expiry and network disconnect clear complete and partial buffers.

final_contract_rereview_status.initial_verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED; preserved as historical exact-freeze review

findings.title: No distinct per-root local desktop preview opt-in
findings.evidence: The proposed setPreviewAccess DTO is {rootId,deviceIds} and persists only allowedPreviewDeviceIds. The contract requires explicit click plus authenticatedLocal but has no desktopPreviewEnabled per-root state or legacy default false. BUILD1 c07_both_app_preview_preflight independently identifies this gap. ROOT decision: desktopPreviewEnabled defaults false and mutation is strict {rootId,desktopPreviewEnabled,deviceIds}.
findings.required_correction: Add a separate persisted desktopPreviewEnabled field; absent legacy state defaults false and is never inferred from browse/mobile grants. Local RPC mutation must strictly carry rootId, desktopPreviewEnabled, and deviceIds.

findings.title: Desktop IPC connection identity is not tied to a main-owned WebContents/navigation incarnation
findings.evidence: The contract models a server-derived connectionId and says extend context if missing, but does not define local IPC identity across renderer navigation/reload or a main-owned WebContents incarnation. Current local catalog IPC supplies authenticatedLocal; WebSocket connection IDs are a separate runtime-RPC concept. A stale renderer request/session could otherwise outlive navigation or bind to a replacement document.
findings.required_correction: Define a main-owned identity bound to the exact WebContents plus navigation/document incarnation, never supplied by renderer parameters; abort/revoke sessions on navigation, destruction, or lifecycle teardown and bind ticket/session checks to that identity.

findings.title: Final authorization proof lacks an explicit epoch/ticket fence at synchronous chunk commit
findings.evidence: The contract requires authorization rechecks before/after awaits and says commit only while the session remains current, but does not define an authority epoch/ticket whose value is compared atomically at the final synchronous offset/output commit against intervening revoke, unpair, permission change, or root replacement.
findings.required_correction: Capture an authority epoch/ticket with the session, refresh it across awaited root/native proofs, and synchronously compare it with current session/authority state at the single-use offset/output commit. A mismatch must emit no chunk and must not advance committed offset.

findings.title: UTF-8 validation is attributed to the server although the contract assigns it to the client
findings.evidence: The opening boundary says the server returns UTF-8 text after complete-file assembly and validation. The DTO actually sends base64 chunks to the client, and the later rule says the client performs fatal UTF-8 decoding after the final chunk; PreviewFinishRequest contains no proof of successful client decoding. Bytes are therefore delivered before final display and the server cannot attest to a client decode.
findings.required_correction: State precisely that the server streams bounded raw bytes as chunks and enforces byte/version/authorization completeness; the client performs fatal UTF-8 decode and displays nothing until success. Do not describe client decode as server validation or claim the server can verify client decoding.

findings.title: Transient CLI and remote runtime-scope denial need explicit user-facing contract wording
findings.evidence: The principal section refuses runtime-scope devices and the body rejects arbitrary remote runtime principals, but it does not explicitly identify transient Unix CLI preview as denied or specify the remote-runtime UI outcome. ROOT decision: transient Unix CLI content preview is denied and runtime-scope remote desktop clients are explicitly denied in UI/docs.
findings.required_correction: Name transient CLI as an unsupported principal and specify that remote runtime-scope clients cannot preview; ensure the UI explains denial and never falls back to worktree files.readPreview.

confirmed_points: Random short-lived entryRef is bound to emitted listing rows, exact components, principal/connection, host, native root identity, generation, entry and stat version; deterministic entryId alone is not authority.
Mobile browse and allowedPreviewDeviceIds are separate, with legacy missing mobile preview grants default denied; principal scope is server-derived and runtime-scope peers are rejected.
Stat version uses full-width decimal metadata and is explicitly not a content digest or privileged-tampering guarantee.

No-follow/nonblocking descriptor traversal, before/after named and opened identity checks, same-device checks, bounded pread, FIFO refusal, descriptor cleanup and confirmed-exit/no-overlap helper behavior are specified.

Chunk sessions enforce ordered offsets, sizes, response limits, no partial render, volatile-only data, content-free logging, invalidation/lease behavior and host/focus fencing. BUILD1 both-app preflight confirms existing UI listing is metadata-only and currently preserves explicit host/root state.

confirmed_corrections.evidence: PreviewFinishResult and PreviewRenewResult carry relative leaseTtlMs. Finish and renew deadlines are computed from the local monotonic start of the corresponding request, capped at 30 seconds; response receipt and server wall time do not extend the lease.

Finish is accepted only when its response arrives before the client-computed deadline. Renew starts only before the current deadline and is accepted only before both existing and proposed deadlines while the preview remains active. Late responses cannot extend or revive expired content; test cases cover wall-clock skew and expiry-before-renew.

Backgrounding, disconnect, navigation, or loss of connection clears displayed content and requires a fresh explicit Preview action; server state is destroyed on close/disconnect/error/invalidation/lease expiry.

The synchronous ticket covers only main-owned root registration/generation and grants, verified pairing/scope, connection lifecycle, and helper incarnation. External note editors do not participate. Final comparison and session/offset/response commit have no intervening await.

Native root/file identity and version checks are explicitly observations at documented read points; they do not make content immutable or guarantee detection of a privileged actor restoring metadata, and already delivered bytes cannot be recalled.

findings.title: Catalog helper containment has a parent-directory TOCTOU race
findings.reproduction: In a disposable temp bundle, monkeypatch os.open so that after _read_regular_beneath has completed lstat/realpath/os.access checks but immediately before the real open, rename the validated Resources/data-catalog directory and replace it with a symlink to a sibling temp directory containing an outside helper with the same filename and byte length. readable_regular_file_ok returned True and the open followed the swapped parent symlink; O_NOFOLLOW protects only the final component.
findings.impact: The gate can accept and read an external helper despite the contract requiring both helpers to be contained beneath Resources with no symlinked parent. Static parent-symlink tests pass but do not cover the swap race.
findings.suggested_fix: Use descriptor-relative traversal from an opened Resources directory with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW for each component, then open the leaf O_NOFOLLOW and validate/read via fstat on the descriptor; add a controlled parent-swap regression.

findings.title: The out/main node budget counts directories but not non-JavaScript file leaves
findings.reproduction: Built a disposable synthetic ASAR with catalog capability absent and 4,097 distinct .json file leaves beneath out/main/assets. catalog_capability returned (False, None) despite MAX_MAIN_GRAPH_NODES=4,096 because _main_js_entries increments nodes for directory recursion only and increments the separate file budget only for JS/CJS/MJS entries.
findings.impact: The declared graph-node budget is not enforced for all graph entries. The independent 16 MiB ASAR-header bound still caps total serialized input, so this reproduction does not establish unbounded memory; it does establish the advertised node cap is incomplete and leaves extra parse/traversal work outside that cap.
findings.suggested_fix: Charge the node budget for every child entry before classifying it, then retain the distinct JavaScript-file and byte budgets; add a non-JS leaf overflow regression.

review_findings: Root and parent traversal uses descriptor-relative opens with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW; each opened directory is checked with fstat and parent-relative no-follow stat. Final preview files use O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and are accepted only when both opened and named snapshots are regular files on the registered root device.

statPreview compares the complete preview identity (dev, ino, sizeBytes, mtimeNs, ctimeNs, fileType) from the opened descriptor and final name against the identity captured at open, then revalidates the root and parent chain. readPreviewChunk checks the requested version before pread and compares complete post-read descriptor/name snapshots and root/parent bindings before returning bytes.

Race controls are supported by deterministic synthetic same-size rewrite tests at both reported interleavings, final-name and parent swaps, and regular-file-to-FIFO replacement; all temporary file and directory descriptors are closed in finally paths. FIFO opens are nonblocking and rejected after fstat.

Native provider root identity is checked against the opened root descriptor and reopened registration path; unsupported/zero provider identities fail closed. The helper DTOs, request/response sizes, path depth/name, open-handle count, file/chunk sizes, decimal fields, expected offsets, and stat-version tokens are bounded/validated.

Transport deadlines reject pending requests and kill only its owned child. Recovery creates a new transport only after confirmed exit; stale handles remain tied to the old epoch, and repeated recovered epochs do not remain retained. Unconfirmed child exit, malformed protocol, and disposal prevent replacement/revival. No content is emitted through logs or arbitrary-path operations.

findings.summary: Authority availability is currently based only on enabled and the original deviceId. Workspace access is reread for paired operations, but it is an async one-shot check; service methods continue after await without verifying the same authority generation/policy snapshot. A workspace/device revocation that lands after canUseWorkspace reads the file but before its caller resumes can pass the old authorization result. Existing project equality checks only detect stored project mutation, not policy-generation change.
findings.required_contract: Represent current authority with a canonical generation/fingerprint (including device identity, project registrations, and workspace grants), capture it during admission, and revalidate the exact generation immediately before every post-await mutation or protected response. Revocation must synchronously make supervisor readiness false and prevent claims. Define explicitly whether an authority/project revocation also persists exact stop intents for already-running attempts; a readiness=false check alone pauses new claims but current runtime continues an active lease until cancellation or expiry.

findings.summary: openStore registers projects once; later configuration changes with the same deviceId do not invalidate authorityAvailable or refresh the existing store registration. Paired workspace authorization checks the current config, but the worker/store project roster remains its initial snapshot unless an explicit refresh/restart policy is applied.
findings.required_contract: Choose and enforce a policy for same-device authority changes: either freeze the complete configuration generation for the lifetime of this authority and require a restart, or atomically refresh the store project roster and invalidate in-flight authorization before continuing. Do not claim live configuration reload from the current enabled/deviceId check.

authority_change_assessment.worker_runtime_behavior: CloudWorkerRuntime.runTick pauses new claims when ready/dispatch authority is false, but it does not automatically stop active workers on authority.ready becoming false; active cancellation follows durable stopping/expiry observations. This is safe only if revocation semantics intentionally mean pause-new-work. Hard revocation needs an explicit exact-lease stop policy, with reservations retained until bound process-stop proof.

finding.summary: CloudJobService.close() synchronously closes and nulls the store without tracking in-flight service operations or marking the service terminal. An operation such as paired submit/get/cancel/retry may be awaiting canUseWorkspace or another async verifier when close runs; its continuation can call the lazy store getter again and reopen the database if authorityAvailable is still true. Current main will-quit barrier does not call CloudJobService.close() or a worker supervisor shutdown because composition is not yet wired.
finding.required_contract: Treat close() as a resource reset only when no operations are in flight; add a separate quiesce/drain/terminal shutdown contract or an operation-generation fence. Shutdown must stop new RPC admission, mark authority/readiness unavailable, await the in-flight supervisor tick, request exact stop intent for active leases, and wait only to the defined bounded deadline. Drain/fence async API operations before closing the shared store. On timeout, retain unresolved lease/capacity/journal evidence and report cleanup unproven; do not reopen the store from a stale continuation or delete reservations. Startup must recover that durable uncertainty before new claims.

recommended_order: Stop new RPC/job mutations and invalidate the authority generation synchronously.
Set dispatch intent false and mark the supervisor shutting down before awaiting.
Await CloudWorkerRuntime.shutdown with a bounded timeout; it waits for the in-flight tick, writes exact stop intent, observes/cancels only exact leases, and retains active slots if stop is uncertain.

Drain or invalidate in-flight CloudJobService operations; close the single shared CloudJobStore only after no callback can use/reopen it. If shutdown times out, preserve durable attempts and reservations for next-start recovery.
At next startup, reopen one store, re-enroll the exact two slots, reconcile journal/lease identity, and expose eligibility only after both slots recover.

findings.summary: The in-process epoch final check does not linearize against external process commits after the final async source reread and before journal/cache publication. Current source surfaces use independent SQLite, SafeJsonFile/root-lock, monitor-process atomic JSON, and live runtime state. A sync per-source revision read can detect earlier commits but not serialize a concurrent external commit. Require a shared cross-process commit fence/lock or state the coordinator only fences enrolled in-process writers and keep all-surface reader unavailable.

The collector double-reads external reservation snapshots only during sampling. Existing claimWorkerJob and authorizeWorkerStart recheck C02 reservation rows inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE but use the earlier capacity sample; they do not read a non-C02 ledger revision/total. Require transaction-scoped external ledger reads used by both paths in the same transaction; avoid a reservation API that opens a nested transaction; prove insert-after-sample and between-claim/start races serialize.

The exact producer set and participation authority are not yet established. Empty ledger means no rows, not no non-C02 disk writers. Coverage must be derived from a main-owned expected participant registry and writer exclusion/participation; arbitrary producer IDs or a self-asserted complete flag cannot make it complete.

findings.detail: Reservation byte overflow is checked only after participant.reserve has already been invoked. For example, a valid pre-summary with reserved bytes in other participants plus an intent that makes the total exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER invokes the target writer, then the post-summary becomes unavailable; the callback may have committed an irreversible reservation. Also, before.reservedBytes + intent.bytes can be unsafe and is rejected only by the postcondition after the callback. Before calling the writer, require safe per-participant and cohort sums (intent.bytes <= MAX_SAFE - before.reservedBytes and, when the numeric cohort total is known, intent.bytes <= MAX_SAFE - current.managedExternalReservedBytes); refuse without callback and without mutating the registry on arithmetic overflow.

The postcondition snapshots only the target participant observation. readSummary tracks prior sourceRevision values for all participants, but it does not compare the full pre/post cohort reservationRevision and reservedBytes (or the other non-sampled observation fields) for non-target participants. If another declared participant changes its reservationRevision/reservedBytes during this target callback while its sourceRevision stays constant, the post-summary can remain available and the target receipt can pass. Capture the pre-callback observation map and require every non-target participant to remain unchanged in scope, generation, sourceRevision, reservationRevision, lifecycle and reservedBytes; otherwise permanently fence and return unknown. Add a deterministic fixture mutating a second participant during target reserve while holding its sourceRevision constant.

incoming-message.ts captures state before inference and writes the captured object afterward. Connection.selectGroups mutates current state and bumps UI revision, but the inference uses current-generation check rather than selection revision/member check. Probe saved a new three-group selection during a deferred reply; completion restored the old selection.

Local disconnect preserves unknown outbox receipts and restore marks prepared sends unknown, preventing blind resend. Real teleproto adapter only searches process-local confirmed IDs and clears them on disconnect; post-restart receipt remains unknown rather than reconciling.

Production main composition supplies null reply and consent adapters; startReplies is not in the shared/preload API nor called at startup. The current ChatConsentProof is sender-scoped and does not establish complete participant set consent; UI states consent pending and disables approve/send.

Successful remote revoke clears account/session/groups/drafts/outbox after draining sends. Decide whether minimal receipt identity must survive account logout/re-auth to prevent loss of ambiguous-send history.

additional_finding.summary: Revoke access after pausing in the same running process fails before remote logout.
additional_finding.reproduction: after restore(), pause(), then restore() on the same TelegramAccountService: restore returns stale-operation because isCurrent requires !paused; subsequent revoke returns client-unavailable and fake revokeAuthorization is not called. The desktop wrapper uses this direct restore path for paused revoke; its existing test covers only a newly constructed post-restart service.
